sources.fact: OS Open UPRN is an open dataset for linking and visualising data related to UPRNs and is updated every six weeks with AddressBase epochs.
UPRNs are authoritative persistent identifiers for addressable locations, primarily allocated by local authorities under their address-maintenance duties.
UPRNs cover approximately 40 million addressable locations and can include non-building objects such as bus shelters or electricity substations.
OS Open UPRN GeoPackage records are point geometries representing the location of the address record, with BNG and latitude/longitude coordinates.
The UPRN persists through address-name, use or demolition-related lifecycle changes and is designed as a dataset-join key.
OS Open UPRN contains the position and unique identifier for records held in AddressBase Premium and supports GIS/spatial-database linkage.
OS Open UPRN is supplied as whole-GB CSV and GeoPackage data; supply format does not convert address points into cadastral polygons.
OS Open Linked Identifiers provides authoritative relationships among UPRNs, USRNs and TOIDs and is updated every six weeks.
UPRN is a persistent reference key for joining related address records across AddressBase products; persistence does not establish legal ownership.
OS NGD address features carry UPRN and lifecycle/version attributes plus address coordinates; identifier linkage remains distinct from HMLR title registration.
Coordinates are address-record locations in BNG/ETRS89, not surveyed legal-boundary vertices.
UPRN-to-TOID/USRN relationships improve data connectivity but are not HMLR title-number relationships.

examples.result: UPRN point is accepted as an addressable-location join anchor only; no buffer/snap is treated as a legal parcel polygon.
Persistent UPRN does not identify the current owner or title number.
A UPRN-to-TOID relationship is not converted to an HMLR title relation.
One development site may contain several UPRNs; no arbitrary merge is made without exact site/title evidence.
An addressable object may be non-residential or even a non-building object, so UPRN existence is not a dwelling/building-use score.
Six-week update cadence supports recency controls but does not prove a candidate-specific join was executed.
Coordinates are not assumed to be building centroids, entrance points or legal boundary vertices beyond the documented address-record location semantics.
No candidate promotion occurs from UPRN linkage without exact HMLR title/parcel relation plus current planning/statutory evidence.
